sections.overview: The inventory name Misumenops nepenthicola is used in ecological studies of a small crab spider living in tropical pitcher plants (Nepenthes).
sections.identification: This is a crab spider (Thomisidae); reliable species-specific measurements and field marks were not established by the sources summarized here.
sections.habitat: Field studies found these spiders in ground-level pitchers of Nepenthes rafflesiana and N. gracilis in Brunei, usually where the pitcher fluid was at an intermediate level.
sections.diet: They take insects caught by the pitcher plant, retrieving prey from the fluid surface; observations also document attacks on visiting insects near pitcher rims.
sections.behavior: Adults are usually solitary and rarely leave their pitchers; they can move between pitchers and cling to the slippery rims using adhesive leg structures.
sections.reproduction: Females attach one or two egg cocoons to the inner pitcher wall, guard the eggs, and provide hatched spiderlings with pre-digested food.
sections.ecology: The spider may benefit the pitcher plant by dropping prey remains into it, but the interaction can also include food theft; studies describe the balance as context-dependent.
sections.conservation: No global assessment for this spider was located; its pitcher-plant habitat is threatened by habitat loss in parts of Southeast Asia.
